title: Democratic stagnation and declining rights are being linked to conflict risk, especially where procedures exist without real competition or enforceable rights
source_unit: International IDEA, The Global State of Democracy 2026: Democracy in an Age of Conflict, 15 September 2026
geography: Countries assessed through the Global State of Democracy Indices, across regions and levels of democratic performance

denominator.unit: International IDEA Global State of Democracy assessment frame

stagnation.value: the report documents democratic stagnation and key declines across election credibility, legislative effectiveness, freedoms of expression and the press, and access to justice

breadth.value: declines affect countries across the spectrum of democratic performance

democratic_route.value: democratic quality is treated as multidimensional institutional capacity rather than the presence of elections alone

observations.method: International IDEA assessment using the latest Global State of Democracy Indices and a dedicated analysis of democracy, conflict, and peace.
observations.uncertainty: Index trends summarize country-level indicators and do not establish a single causal pathway from democratic decline to every conflict, rights, or welfare outcome.
observations.subgroup: Citizens, voters, legislatures, courts, journalists, civil-society organizations, opposition groups, and governments across assessed countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Institutional decline can be uneven, reversible, or offset by civic action, local governance, constitutional safeguards, or reforms not visible in aggregate trends.

procedural_gap.value: countries with some democratic procedures but without real political competition or enforceable rights are identified as a distinct risk context

rights_route.value: political competition, rights enforcement, expression, press freedom, legislative effectiveness, and justice access jointly shape democratic legitimacy

legitimacy_test.value: the presence of formal institutions is insufficient if citizens cannot use them to contest power or secure rights

observations.method: International IDEA comparative democracy assessment and analysis of institutional dimensions associated with conflict.
observations.uncertainty: The report’s cross-country relationships do not predict individual political experiences or identify which reform will restore competition and enforceability in each setting.
observations.subgroup: Citizens with unequal access to political voice, journalists, opposition parties, courts, minorities, and communities exposed to repression or exclusion.
observations.counterinterpretation: Partial democratic procedures may still provide meaningful channels for reform, negotiation, and peaceful contestation even when rights enforcement is weak.

conflict_context.value: the report states that violent conflict is more prevalent than at any time in the past 80 years and places the democracy-conflict relationship in renewed focus

association.value: contexts of nondemocracy and democratic decline are associated with more violent conflict in the report’s analysis

security_route.value: democratic governance quality becomes part of conflict prevention and peace-building infrastructure

observations.method: International IDEA comparative analysis of Global State of Democracy indicators alongside interstate and intrastate conflict patterns.
observations.uncertainty: Association is not proof that democratic decline causes each conflict; conflict can also erode institutions, and omitted geopolitical, economic, and historical factors matter.
observations.subgroup: Conflict-affected populations, political institutions, security actors, civil society, international mediators, and states undergoing democratic regression.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some autocratic or hybrid settings may suppress visible conflict temporarily, while democratic competition can itself be destabilizing without institutional safeguards.

denominator.unit: International IDEA policy and reform frame

recession.value: the report describes a continuing democratic recession and warns that declining governance quality raises concerns about the likelihood of conflict

reform_need.value: reversing negative trends requires attention to credible elections, effective legislatures, expression and press freedoms, justice access, and enforceable rights

open_test.value: connect democracy indicators to actual protection, public-system performance, civic participation, and peace outcomes without treating rankings as destiny

observations.method: International IDEA report synthesis and policy recommendations based on the Global State of Democracy Indices and democracy-conflict analysis.
observations.uncertainty: Recommendations do not establish political feasibility, implementation sequence, or distribution of benefits across countries and groups.
observations.subgroup: Reformers, political parties, legislatures, courts, media, civic organizations, international organizations, and communities seeking accountable government.
observations.counterinterpretation: Institutional reform can be context-specific; external democracy templates may fail without local legitimacy, resources, and security.

related_sources.claim: CIVICUS civil-society reporting provides complementary evidence on civic-space pressure and collective resistance.
WTO trade-governance analysis provides complementary institutional and geopolitical cooperation context.

boundary: This record adds a democracy-to-conflict route from institutional credibility, competition, rights, expression, and justice through legitimacy and peace. It uses comparative index and report analysis, not individual political histories, causal conflict attribution, public-opinion representativeness, or proof that any ranking determines future outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official International IDEA publication page was reviewed for democratic stagnation, indicator declines, cross-performance breadth, democracy-conflict associations, democratic recession, publication date, and reform framing.
